22mar.summary: Henry Brooke, Lord Cobham, one of Elizabeth's peace commissioners at Ostend in spring 1588, asks that ships be sent to attend on the coast, warns that the garrison is too weak and short of money and victuals, and reports Parma's new ditch from Ghent by Eeclo to Sluys, nearly navigable for his float-boats, and the threat to the town and haven. No sign-level transcription exists: the cipher runs were read word by word from crops of the DECODE images.

middelburg.summary: An enclosed intelligence report in another hand: Grenier's intrigue in clear, then in cipher advice that the ships be well guarded with two or three pinnaces in the channel, and news that a Jesuit (surname read Bastune?) has been sent post into Italy. No sign-level transcription exists.

20mar.summary: Cobham reports new companies at Oudenburg and stone and fagots coming by water from Eeclo, suspects an attempt on Ostend and asks to be removed to a safer place; he would think himself unhappy to be a means to conclude an irreligious peace, and argues against handing the prisoners Pigot and Barney over to the States. No sign-level transcription exists.

system: Graphic-sign simple substitution with a few homophones (a, i/a, w/u, g), words divided, inserted as runs in clear English.
